name: manifest-dev
description: Manifest-driven development: /figure-out reaches shared understanding, /define writes Deliverables with Acceptance Criteria and Global Invariants, and /do implements them. Each gate is one text — a title, a body, and an optional why — carrying a required kind (judgment or deterministic, never inferred) as its only structured metadata; execution policy is selected at /do launch as per-gate (independent default), consolidated, or self, with an optional verifier model for independent modes. Every mode keeps a provenance-rich gate ledger and the run never downgrades itself. Re-verification follows each gate's declared kind: command-backed gates re-run in full, while judgment gates take one full look and then judge only prior findings' repairs and the changed delta, with --exhaustive-verification restoring full re-sampling. A default-on execution log preserves deviations and dead-end memory; --no-log opts out. For unattended runs, use a host-native goal-setting backstop whose completion contract requires fresh PASS evidence for every gate under the selected mode. /auto chains the full flow, and /figure-out-team extends deliberation to multi-party Slack sessions. /ticket-up authors convention-compliant Tickets from a Manifest, direct work, independently managed questions, or source-linked follow-ups; one Manifest becomes one coherent Shaped Ticket by default, with Deliverable splitting reserved for explicit delegation. Follow-up Auto preserves source authority for unattended or nested authoring, while a person at the ticket-up boundary may freshly grant Auto after the new Ticket independently qualifies. /next-ticket claims and presents the ready Ticket whose delay would lose the most project value for the human-plus-AI session, using current executor time rather than traditional feature-size estimates. /run-ticket receives one exact Ticket, recovers its stable branch and pull request, invokes /auto, completes required landing, and records DONE or ESCALATED on that Ticket. /sweep-tickets recovers first or starts one eligible Auto Ticket by the same delay-loss objective per scheduled invocation. Stores use the project's shared tracker, GitHub Issues out of the box, or files where cross-checkout claiming is not needed. figure-out speaks to one reader with limited attention — state at a glance, one slot per set member so a dropped one shows, the ask set apart — with form otherwise its own call. /just-figure-out and /just-define are the lean arm of the same beats: goal-based investigation and Manifest encoding with minimal process, fully self-contained, chaining to /just-do and chained end-to-end by /just-auto. /init-context sets a repository up with the surfaces the workflow reads from — a North Star (the project's standing strategy surface: nine fields from diagnosis to never-does, every position carrying a dated state of evidence, hypothesis, ruled, or empty, informing every session and never binding, with positions changed only by the owner's ruling), project-owned ADR conventions, a glossary, and the context-file wiring that keeps sessions using all of them — seeding them from the project's own history where there is any; re-running it compares the project-owned copies it wrote — forks no sync updates — against the current defaults and offers each difference for the user to take or leave. figure-out's docs mode keeps the North Star current under its update asymmetry and notes when a recorded decision sits outside what the Diagnosis names, since a position also goes stale by drifting out of date while nothing contradicts it, /define's marketing task file gates outward-facing claims against its Promise and Never, and /next-ticket weighs cross-effort priority against its winning definition. Prose deliverables are gated by register: a shared floor plus one register overlay — documentation (DOCS-STYLE-REFERENCE) or human-voiced writing (WRITING-REFERENCE) — which never compose together, so no deliverable loads two contradictory rules. /review-writing applies the same standards to any text on demand, outside a manifest run.
